views.name: users_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "first_name" AS first_name,
       "last_name" AS last_name,
       "email" AS email,
       "age" AS age,
       "gender" AS gender,
       "state" AS state,
       "street_address" AS street_address,
       "postal_code" AS postal_code,
       "city" AS city,
       "country" AS country,
       "latitude" AS latitude,
       "longitude" AS longitude,
       "traffic_source" AS traffic_source,
       "created_at" AS created_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS
views.description: Canonical cleaned USERS projection. Use this when joining or filtering users to ensure consistent column names, normalized geolocation and account timestamps. | Use for: User-level cohorts or demographics; Joining user attributes to orders/events; Filtering active users by created_at or traffic_source

views.name: products_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "cost" AS cost,
       "category" AS category,
       "name" AS name,
       "brand" AS brand,
       "retail_price" AS retail_price,
       "department" AS department,
       "sku" AS sku,
       "distribution_center_id" AS distribution_center_id
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
views.description: Clean PRODUCTS projection with consistent column aliases for joins to order items or inventory. Use when product attributes and prices are needed. | Use for: Product-level revenue/cost analysis; Joining product metadata to order items or inventory

views.name: inventory_items_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "product_id" AS product_id,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "sold_at" AS sold_at,
       "cost" AS cost,
       "product_category" AS product_category,
       "product_name" AS product_name,
       "product_brand" AS product_brand,
       "product_retail_price" AS product_retail_price,
       "product_department" AS product_department,
       "product_sku" AS product_sku,
       "product_distribution_center_id" AS product_distribution_center_id
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS
grain: one row per physical inventory item
views.description: Clean INVENTORY_ITEMS projection at the per-item grain, exposing product attributes and sold_at timestamp for inventory or cost analysis. | Use for: Inventory turnover and sold vs unsold item counts; Per-item cost and margin when joined to order items

views.name: orders_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "order_id" AS order_id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "status" AS status,
       "gender" AS gender,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "returned_at" AS returned_at,
       "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       "num_of_item" AS num_of_item
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
views.description: Canonical ORDERS projection (order header) exposing core timestamps and status for joins and aggregation. | Use for: Order-level funnel and status distributions; Join to order_items for line-level analysis

views.name: order_items_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "order_id" AS order_id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "product_id" AS product_id,
       "inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
       "status" AS status,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       "returned_at" AS returned_at,
       "sale_price" AS sale_price
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
grain: one row per order line item
views.description: Canonical ORDER_ITEMS projection at order-line grain, retaining foreign keys and sale price timestamps for revenue/fulfillment analysis. | Use for: Line-item revenue, returns, and fulfillment metrics; Linking sold inventory items to order lines

views.name: events_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "sequence_number" AS sequence_number,
       "session_id" AS session_id,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "ip_address" AS ip_address,
       "city" AS city,
       "state" AS state,
       "postal_code" AS postal_code,
       "browser" AS browser,
       "traffic_source" AS traffic_source,
       "uri" AS uri,
       "event_type" AS event_type
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS
views.description: Canonical EVENTS projection with session and event metadata, suitable for behavioral funnels and sessionization. | Use for: Sessionization, event funnels, and traffic_source attribution; Joining events to users to enrich behavior with demographics

views.name: distribution_centers_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "name" AS name,
       "latitude" AS latitude,
       "longitude" AS longitude
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.DISTRIBUTION_CENTERS
views.description: Simple projection of DISTRIBUTION_CENTERS for geographic joins to products or inventory items. | Use for: Mapping inventory/products to distribution centers; Geographic nearest-center calculations when joined with user locations

views.name: orders_per_user_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT "user_id" AS user_id,
       COUNT(DISTINCT "order_id") AS orders_count,
       SUM("num_of_item") AS total_items_ordered,
       MIN("created_at") AS first_order_at,
       MAX("created_at") AS last_order_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
GROUP BY "user_id"
views.description: Aggregated order-level metrics per user: counts of orders and sum of items. Use for user-level activity scoring and join to user demographics. | Use for: User segmentation by ordering frequency; Churn/retention analysis using first/last order timestamps

views.name: revenue_per_product_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT "product_id" AS product_id,
       COUNT(1) AS units_sold,
       SUM("sale_price") AS gross_revenue,
       AVG("sale_price") AS avg_sale_price,
       MIN("created_at") AS first_sale_at,
       MAX("created_at") AS last_sale_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
GROUP BY "product_id"
grain: one row per product_id aggregated across order lines
views.description: Aggregates revenue and units sold at the product_id level from ORDER_ITEMS. Use for top-sellers and product-level revenue analysis. | Use for: Top-selling products, revenue trends by product; Joining product revenue to product metadata for margin calculations

views.name: order_items_with_product_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT oi."id" AS id,
       oi."order_id" AS order_id,
       oi."user_id" AS user_id,
       oi."product_id" AS product_id,
       p."category" AS product_category,
       p."name" AS product_name,
       p."brand" AS product_brand,
       p."retail_price" AS product_retail_price,
       oi."sale_price" AS sale_price,
       oi."created_at" AS created_at,
       oi."shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       oi."delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       oi."returned_at" AS returned_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi
LEFT JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS p
  ON oi."product_id" = p."id"
grain: one row per order line with product metadata
views.description: Denormalized order-line view joining ORDER_ITEMS to PRODUCTS to provide product metadata next to sale_price. Useful for product-level revenue by category or brand. | Use for: Revenue by product category or brand; Return rates by product attributes

views.name: order_items_with_inventory_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT oi."id" AS id,
       oi."order_id" AS order_id,
       oi."user_id" AS user_id,
       oi."product_id" AS product_id,
       oi."inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
       ii."cost" AS inventory_cost,
       ii."product_sku" AS inventory_sku,
       ii."product_distribution_center_id" AS product_distribution_center_id,
       oi."sale_price" AS sale_price,
       oi."created_at" AS created_at,
       ii."sold_at" AS item_sold_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi
LEFT JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS ii
  ON oi."inventory_item_id" = ii."id"
grain: one row per order line enriched with inventory item when available
views.description: Join ORDER_ITEMS to INVENTORY_ITEMS when inventory_item_id is present to connect specific sold item attributes (cost, distribution center). Useful for per-item margin and fulfillment tracing. | Use for: Per-item margin = sale_price - inventory_cost; Trace fulfillment center for specific sold items

views.name: latest_event_per_session_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "id" AS id,
  "user_id" AS user_id,
  "session_id" AS session_id,
  "sequence_number" AS sequence_number,
  "created_at" AS created_at,
  "event_type" AS event_type,
  "uri" AS uri,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "session_id" ORDER BY "sequence_number" DESC, "created_at" DESC) AS event_rank
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS
grain: one row per event with rank within session
views.description: Windowed relation ranking events per session by sequence_number and created_at. Use to select latest or first event per session by filtering on event_rank. | Use for: Get first/last event per session; Session-level funnel steps using event_rank

views.name: user_sessions_event_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT "user_id" AS user_id,
       "session_id" AS session_id,
       COUNT(1) AS events_in_session,
       MIN("created_at") AS session_start_at,
       MAX("created_at") AS session_end_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS
GROUP BY "user_id", "session_id"
views.description: Counts events per user-session and exposes first/last event times. Useful for session length and engagement metrics. | Use for: Sessionization metrics and average events per session; Join to orders to attribute conversions to sessions

views.name: top_products_by_revenue_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT oi."product_id" AS product_id,
       SUM(oi."sale_price") AS gross_revenue,
       COUNT(1) AS units_sold,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(oi."sale_price") DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi
GROUP BY oi."product_id"
grain: one row per product aggregated with revenue and rank
views.description: Ranks products by gross revenue using ORDER_ITEMS. Downstream queries can filter rank <= K to get top-K products. | Use for: Top-K products by revenue; Product ranking by units or revenue when adjusted

views.name: running_revenue_by_day_win
views.body_sql:
SELECT day_epoch,
       daily_revenue,
       SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY day_epoch ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT CAST(FLOOR("created_at"/86400) AS NUMBER) AS day_epoch,
         SUM("sale_price") AS daily_revenue
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
  GROUP BY CAST(FLOOR("created_at"/86400) AS NUMBER)
) sub
grain: one row per epoch-day with daily and running revenue
views.description: Daily gross revenue (from ORDER_ITEMS.created_at as epoch) with running total ordered by day. Use for cumulative revenue charts. Note: does not bucket into calendar dates — downstream should convert epoch to DATE if needed. | Use for: Cumulative revenue over time; Daily revenue trends and moving totals

views.name: users_with_order_metrics_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT users_cte.id AS id,
       users_cte.email AS email,
       users_cte.age AS age,
       users_cte.gender AS gender,
       users_cte.city AS city,
       users_cte.country AS country,
       orders_agg.orders_count AS orders_count,
       orders_agg.total_items_ordered AS total_items_ordered,
       orders_agg.first_order_at AS first_order_at,
       orders_agg.last_order_at AS last_order_at
FROM (
  SELECT "id" AS id,
         "email" AS email,
         "age" AS age,
         "gender" AS gender,
         "city" AS city,
         "country" AS country
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS
) users_cte
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT "user_id" AS user_id,
         COUNT(DISTINCT "order_id") AS orders_count,
         SUM("num_of_item") AS total_items_ordered,
         MIN("created_at") AS first_order_at,
         MAX("created_at") AS last_order_at
  FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
  GROUP BY "user_id"
) orders_agg
  ON users_cte.id = orders_agg.user_id
grain: one row per user enriched with order aggregates
views.description: User-level denormalized view joining USERS to aggregated order metrics (orders_per_user_agg). Useful for segmentation and retention modelling. | Use for: User segmentation, lifetime value proxies, retention cohorts
